{{Short description|International prize for mathematicians}}
The '''International János Bolyai Prize of Mathematics''' is an international prize founded by the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. The prize is named after [[János Bolyai]] and is awarded every five years<ref>Szénássy B.: Adalékok a Bolyai-díj történetéhez, ''Természet Világa'', '''124'''(1993),7, 291&ndash;294. </ref> to [[mathematician]]s for [[monograph]]s with important new results in the preceding 10 years.

== Medalists ==
* 1905 – {{flagicon|France}} [[Henri Poincaré]]
* 1910 – {{flagicon|Germany|empire}} [[David Hilbert]]
* 2000 – {{flagicon|Israel}} [[Saharon Shelah]] for his ''Cardinal Arithmetic'', Oxford University Press, 1994. {{ISBN|0198537859}}<ref>{{Cite web| title = Laudation of Shelah on the occasion of winning the Bolyai Prize (in Hungarian)| url = https://www.renyi.hu/~csirmaz/shelah/sh.pdf}}</ref><ref name=Totik/>
* 2005 – {{flagicon|Russia}} {{flagicon|France}} [[Mikhail Gromov (mathematician)|Mikhail Gromov]] for his ''Metric Structures for Riemannian and Non-Riemannian Spaces'', Birkhäuser, 1999. {{ISBN|0817638989}}<ref name=Totik/>
* 2010 – {{flagicon|Russia}} {{flagicon|Germany}} [[Yuri I. Manin]] for his ''Frobenius Manifolds, Quantum Cohomology, and Moduli Spaces'', American Mathematical Society, 1999. {{ISBN|0821819178}}<ref>{{Cite web | title = Hungarian Academy of Sciences presents the János Bolyai International Mathematical Prize | url = http://www.math.bme.hu/akademia/jbimp.html | accessdate = 1 April 2010 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20110718044545/http://www.math.bme.hu/akademia/jbimp.html | archivedate = 18 July 2011 }}</ref><ref name=Totik/>
* 2015 – {{flagicon|USA}} {{flagicon|Israel}} [[Barry Simon]] for his ''Orthogonal Polynomials on the Unit Circle'', American Mathematical Society, 2005. {{ISBN|9780821834466}}<ref>[http://mta.hu/news_and_views/mta-international-bolyai-prize-goes-to-barry-simon-135978/''Bolyai Prize goes to Barry Simon''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222174649/http://mta.hu/news_and_views/mta-international-bolyai-prize-goes-to-barry-simon-135978 |date=2015-12-22 }} Communication by [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (mta.hu). Retrieved 12 April 2015</ref><ref name=Totik>{{cite journal | last=Totik | first=V. | title=Barry Simon and the János Bolyai International Mathematical Prize | journal=Acta Mathematica Hungarica | volume=149 | issue=2 | date=2016 | issn=0236-5294 | doi=10.1007/s10474-016-0618-x | pages=263–273 | url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10474-016-0618-x | access-date=2025-12-25| url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* 2020 – {{flagicon|Australia}}{{flagicon|America}} [[Terence Tao]] for his ''Nonlinear Dispersive Equations: Local and Global Analysis'', American Mathematical Society, 2006. {{ISBN|9780821841433}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mta.hu/kozgyules2021/terence-tao-a-bolyai-janos-nemzetkozi-matematikai-dij-2020-as-kituntetettje-111397|title=Terence Tao is the 2020 winner of the János Bolyai International Mathematical Prize (in Hungarian)|author=Hungarian Academy of Sciences|date=3 May 2021|accessdate=8 August 2021}}</ref>
* 2025 – {{flagicon|Hungary}} [[János Kollár]] for his ''Families of Varieties of General Type'', Cambridge University Press, 2023. {{ISBN|9781009346115}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mta.hu/english/janos-kollar-external-member-of-the-hungarian-academy-of-sciences-awarded-the-janos-bolyai-international-mathematics-award-114313|title=János Kollár, external member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, awarded the János Bolyai International Mathematics Award|author=Hungarian Academy of Sciences|date=7 April 2025|accessdate=3 September 2025}}</ref>
